title: Entities
description: Canonical registry of all entities (people, threads, orgs) tracked in the workspace. Source of truth. Markdown views (PEOPLE.md, MASTER_TRACKER.md) are regenerated from this file.

version.description: Monotonically incremented on every write. Used for optimistic concurrency.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 datetime (workspace-local, no timezone suffix). e.g., 2026-04-20T14:32:00

last_writer.description: Name of the skill that performed the last write.

engagements.description: Non-ownership relationships between orgs (fund engagements, portfolio links, deals, advisory, vendor, etc.). Optional. Distinct from org.parent_org_id which encodes ownership only.

workspace.description: Per-workspace settings: user_id, user_timezone, first_go_months, etc. Optional but, when present, consumed by tz.py / people_writer.py / org_writer.py / workspace-manager.

brand.description: OPTIONAL, DORMANT-BY-DEFAULT deliverable theme (SPEC OUT1). A PARTIAL override deep-merged over shared/scripts/brand.py DEFAULT_BRAND at render time — every key is optional and an omitted key keeps the (premium) default. An ABSENT brand object = byte-stable defaults, no warning, no event. NOTHING in onboarding sets this; it is written by hand into a client's entities.json during a paid customization engagement — on the top-level `workspace` object (all that client's docs) or on a single `org` (that org's docs only, overriding the workspace brand). Colors are 6-hex WITHOUT '#'. Fonts are NAMES only and must be installed on the reader's machine.

fonts.description: Font NAME overrides — must be installed on the reader's machine (a downloadable/custom font that isn't present will silently fall back in Word).

footer_line.description: Centered footer text. Defaults to 'Command Room'. NEVER provenance metadata (CONTRACT Rule 15).

logo_path.description: Path to a letterhead image (absolute, or relative to workspace root). Renders right-aligned <= 0.35in at the top of the document ONLY if the file exists; a missing file silently falls back to the quiet no-logo header (R26). Null (default) = no logo.

id.description: Stable identifier. Never reused. Format: person_001, person_002, ...

canonical_name.description: Full first + last name, title case. Source of truth for display.

aliases.description: Name-resolution corpus — every string a user might type that should resolve to this person. Used by workspace-manager / transcript-search / aliases.json reverse lookup.

nicknames.description: Informal display variants (v3.13.0+). Distinct from `aliases`: nicknames is for display/quick-reference; aliases is the search corpus. Most consumers want both flattened together via the get_person_display_names() helper.

primary_org_id.description: The org this person primarily belongs to. Drives affiliation-aware name resolution.

affiliation_ids.description: All orgs this person is affiliated with (board roles, co-ownership, cross-company). Primary is usually also listed here.

email.description: DEPRECATED v3.13.0+. Use `emails` array. Kept for back-compat reads. New writers prefer `emails`; readers use the get_person_emails() helper which merges both.

emails.description: Canonical email shape (v3.13.0+). Array of all known email addresses for this person, work + personal. Use get_person_emails() to read.

phones.description: Phone numbers (v3.13.0+). Array — no singular equivalent.

project_ids.description: Threads this person is involved in.

last_touched_at.description: ISO datetime of the most recent write/touch on this record. Bumped by intro-broker when an intro_made event fires. Optional.

cadence_override_days.description: Phase 6 Quick Win B. User-taught cadence baseline in days. The (now RETIRED — SPEC LIFECYCLE1) Pulse chat's 'just busy' reply (dont_forget_feedback) widened it via dormancy.record_just_busy so dormancy math (dormancy.effective_baseline) stops re-flagging a gap the CEO has said is normal for this person. Absent on legacy records (reads as no override). Optional.

tie.description: SPEC BAL1 D1. Work/personal partition line. Absent means WORK (back-compat). tie=personal people are read ONLY by the Balance surface: dormancy.emit_dormancy_signal refuses them at the shared emit chokepoint (SPEC LIFECYCLE1 moved that gate out of the retired Pulse chat's prose and into code), relationship-moves drops them at the load/score boundary, and the secondary dormancy emitters (team-intelligence, dormant-customer-scan) skip them at their emit gates. NOT `relationship_type` — that name is forbidden (org-level). Optional.

cadence_days.description: SPEC BAL1 D1(b). Personal RE-SURFACE interval in days (date-night cadence for a spouse, call cadence for a parent) — read ONLY by shared/scripts/balance.py. The OPPOSITE of cadence_override_days (dormancy's max-widening suppression knob): this one GENERATES a reconnect nudge when the gap exceeds it. Never routed through dormancy.effective_baseline. Meaningful only with tie=personal. Optional.

connections.description: Optional relationship-graph edges between this person and others. Currently written by intro-broker when an intro_made event fires (one entry per intro, on both sides). Per WORKSPACE_API.md, the connections[] sub-array is namespaced to intro-broker — no collision with people-crm.

needs_enrichment.description: Provisional record awaiting the people-crm enrichment pull (deep-audit #21). The on-entity enrichment flag; cleared (false) after enriching. Replaces the forbidden pending_review/inferred_from on-entity trigger.

project.description: A tracked unit of attention (a 'thread'). User-facing language is 'thread'; the 'project_' id prefix is historical. See 'kind' for the full taxonomy.

folder_name.description: Exact folder name under workspace root (nested 'Parent/Child' allowed). Kinds without a filesystem presence may use a logical name. null when no real directory matches — the canonical writer resolves this against disk and refuses to guess a slug (FOLDERGUARD).

canonical_name.description: The thread's name as the CEO says it. Present on every live thread and allowed by thread_writer since it shipped; declared here 2026-07-25 (it was allowed-but-undeclared, the same drift class as the field additions below). Readers resolve canonical_name first and fall back to display_name.

status.description: Project lifecycle state. v2.10.3+ adds 'dormant' between active and archived: real activity but quiet for 30+ days. Don't Forget proposes the active→dormant transition at 30d and auto-flips at 60d if no user action. Dormant projects are accessible by name (go [project]) but invisible in daily flows. Re-opening a dormant project (go [project] + adding a session note) auto-revives to active. 2026-07-25: 'exploring' / 'scoping' / 'resolved' declared here to match thread_writer.VALID_STATUSES, which has accepted them since it shipped — the enum, not the writer, was the stale side.

affiliation_id.description: DEPRECATED alias of org_id (ENTITY1). Tolerated on records that already carry it and read as a fallback; never newly written — the writer normalises it to org_id.

org_id.description: The org this thread belongs to (most specific level, e.g. org_acme_restaurant rather than the holding org_acme_co) — the canonical thread→org field (ENTITY1). Required at creation: 'personal' EXPLICITLY for a deliberately unaffiliated thread, so 'never set' stays distinguishable from a choice.

parent_thread_id.description: Parent thread if this is a nested thread (replaces subproject model). Must reference an existing project id; no cycles.

spawned_from_thread_id.description: Lineage: the thread from which this one was spawned. Informational; not a hierarchy.

cross_refs.description: Soft links to other threads that are related without being hierarchical.

kind.description: The semantic kind of this thread. SPEC COACH1 §4.1 adds 'coaching' (one coaching engagement with one client — the arc a coach reads) and 'cohort' (a group/peer-group engagement with a roster; carries the `cohort` sub-object below). Widening only — no existing kind changed meaning, and no reader keys off the enum's length.

last_activity.description: DEPRECATED (v4.5.2, F-54/F-61): no writer maintains this field — an ingest-era stamp. Never rank or compute staleness from it; derive recency from events via shared/scripts/thread_activity.py. Zero-event fallback only.

session_count.description: Number of sessions this project has been touched in. Maintained by workspace-manager.

dormancy_reviewed_at.description: ISO datetime of the last time insight-generator's Pass 7 connector probe ran against this project. Used to gate the 14-day re-probe cooldown. Optional.

paused_at.description: When this thread was paused — the pair-mate of archived_at for status='paused'. User-authored; no code reader today.

paused_by.description: Who paused this thread — the pair-mate of archive_reason for status='paused'. User-authored; no code reader today.

key_contact_id.description: Person id of the main contact for this thread. Read by build_workspace_map_input (which also tolerates the legacy spelling primary_contact_id) and by transcript-search's project scoping.

notes.description: Free-text context on the thread. Read by build_workspace_map_input (the map's project line) and build_dcc_input (first sentence as the next_action fallback).

roster_overrides.description: Pin/suppress overrides applied on top of the derived thread roster (thread_roster.derive_roster). Allowed by thread_writer since the brain-substrate fix; declared here 2026-07-25.

deal.description: SPEC PIPE1 (v4.8): sales-deal fields, allowed ONLY on kind='deal' threads (thread_writer rejects it elsewhere). Namespaced so deal.stage (sales stage, string enum) never collides with the integer project-lifecycle `stage`. Written ONLY by shared/scripts/deal_state.py — the single writer/closure path; hand edits are the bug class the typed writers exist to kill. Consistency rules enforced in code: outcome='lost' requires a loss_reason; outcome is terminal and set only by deal_state.close_deal (won → thread status 'resolved', lost → 'archived'). `value` is user-stated or user-confirmed money — NEVER estimated (quantify.py discipline); absent value renders no money tag. Recency/rot derive from events via thread_activity — nothing here stores activity.

value.description: Deal value in `currency`. User-stated or confirmed only; never estimated. Null = unknown (ranges are out of v1 scope — store null + a note in `source`).

stage.description: Active sales stage (fixed v1 set). Won/lost are NOT stages — they are the terminal `outcome`.

stage_entered.description: Date the current stage was entered. Stamped by deal_state.set_stage; resets on every move, including backward moves.

forecast_category.description: Categorical forecast judgment per deal (weighted-pipeline math is statistically meaningless at 5-50 deals; the haircut number is a secondary tile at most).

source.description: Free text — where the deal came from (e.g. 'referral — Bowie'). Also holds value-range notes.

outcome.description: Terminal. Set only by deal_state.close_deal — never hand-written, never a stage.

objective.description: SPEC OBJ1 (draft): standing-objective fields, allowed ONLY on kind='objective' threads (thread_writer rejects it elsewhere). An objective is a CEO-level standing priority — too big to mark done in a day, spanning weeks, tracked through ONE of three bindings the CEO picks (meeting / self / activity). Written ONLY by shared/scripts/objective_state.py — the single writer/closure path (mirrors deal_state doctrine). Directional status is NEVER stored here — it derives from objective_review / objective_report / linked-entity events via shared/scripts/objective_math.py. Consistency rules enforced in code: binding.type determines which binding fields are required; outcome is terminal and set only by objective_state.complete_objective / archive_objective (completed → thread status 'resolved', archived → 'archived').

statement.description: The objective in the CEO's own plain words (e.g. 'Land three enterprise pilots'). Doubles as the topical match surface for relevance capture (alias-style matching via entity_resolve).

horizon.description: Target date, or null for an open horizon. Never used to fabricate a status — display and drift context only.

binding.description: HOW this objective is tracked — the one deliberate choice the CEO makes at creation (the three-way toggle). The system proposes the target inside the chosen path; the CEO confirms. Exactly one binding per objective in v1.

type.description: meeting = reviewed in a recurring meeting (status harvested from its transcripts); self = owner reports in the weekly objectives touch; activity = derived from linked threads'/deals' own events.

series_key.description: meeting binding only: normalized title of the recurring meeting (the series fingerprint). There is no calendar series id in the substrate — title(+people) matching is the established recurrence convention.

series_match.description: meeting binding only: how the series fingerprint matches a processed transcript. title_and_people (default) = normalized title plus usual-attendee overlap; title_only = distinctive unique names (e.g. a named leadership call) where attendee churn must not break the match. Proposed automatically: title unique in meeting history → title_only, generic title → title_and_people.

series_people.description: meeting binding only: person_ids of the usual attendees, used when series_match='title_and_people'.

cadence_days.description: self binding only: expected days between self-reports (default 7 — the weekly objectives touch). Drift math counts missed cycles against this.

entity_ids.description: activity binding only: the linked thread/deal ids whose OWN events drive status. Topic over party — always threads or deals, never a bare person (party overlap is not a join).

target_note.description: activity binding only, optional: plain-text description of the concrete target (e.g. 'deal reaches negotiating', '3 pilots signed'). Display/context only in v1 — a directional status still requires an unambiguous signal (deal stage/outcome), never a parsed guess from this text.

anchor_thread_id.description: Optional link to the existing project/deal thread this objective is about (any binding type). The topical join relevance capture uses: events attributed to the anchor (or to activity-binding entity_ids) count as movement on the objective. Cold-start proposals set this instead of mutating the existing thread's kind.

milestones.description: Optional light step list — display and progress context only, never a status source. No per-step chores: steps flip via the same confirmation surfaces, not scheduled prompts.

outcome.description: Terminal. Set only by objective_state.complete_objective / archive_objective — never hand-written (completed → thread status 'resolved', archived → 'archived').

outcome_note.description: Optional one-liner recorded at close (why archived / what completing looked like).

is_primary_focus.description: LEGACY-TOLERATED, never written (thread_writer.LEGACY_THREAD_FIELDS). This is an ORG field — every reader takes it off an org record. Pre-writer ingest copied it onto 21 live threads, inconsistently (three sibling threads of one org carry different values). Tolerated so those records round-trip; a thread bubbles up via its org, never a thread-side copy.

last_writer.description: LEGACY-TOLERATED, never written (thread_writer.LEGACY_THREAD_FIELDS). This is the entities.json ENVELOPE field set by _save_entities; it leaked onto one thread record from a prose write. Not a thread field.

created_at.description: LEGACY-TOLERATED, never written (thread_writer.LEGACY_THREAD_FIELDS). Creation provenance belongs in the thread_created event — but THREE of the four live threads carrying this (project_020, project_021, project_026) have NO such event, so it is their only record of when they were created. Preserved for that reason; new threads get the event instead. Was FORBIDDEN (silently dropped) until 2026-07-25, which destroyed it on any unrelated update. (project_019 is the fourth and DOES have a thread_created event; the first survey missed it because pre-writer rows carry the thread id at top-level primary_thread_id, not under data.primary_thread_id — survey both shapes.)

created_by.description: LEGACY-TOLERATED, never written (thread_writer.LEGACY_THREAD_FIELDS). Same story as created_at — the only creation provenance those three records have.

aliases.description: LEGACY-TOLERATED, never written (thread_writer.LEGACY_THREAD_FIELDS). Threads have no alias resolver: entity_resolve builds its corpus from person.aliases and org.aliases and matches threads on canonical_name only. Present on the workspace_mini test fixture; absent from every live thread. Declare a resolver before making this canonical.

cohort.description: SPEC COACH1 §4.2: group/peer-group engagement fields, allowed ONLY on kind='cohort' threads (thread_writer rejects it elsewhere). Follows the deal/objective sub-object shape exactly. A group is a book of business with a ROSTER — `stakeholder_person_ids` is insufficient because each seat carries its own state (when they joined, whether they're paused, who pays for them). Read ONLY through shared/scripts/coach_state.py; the pack's writers are the only writers. NOTHING derived is stored here: session counts, arc items, billable tallies and renewal windows are all computed from events, never stamped (the `last_activity` lesson).

cadence.description: How often this cohort meets. Drives the scheduled prep/capture passes. 'other' when the real cadence doesn't fit — the interval then lives in the coach's own directives, not here.

seat_count.description: CONTRACTED seats — what the coach sold, which legitimately differs from how many are currently filled (a departed member frees a seat that is still paid for, or still being sold). It is NOT a cached len(members): occupancy derives from `members` via coach_state.cohort_roster, which returns seats_contracted AND seats_filled side by side and never reconciles one into the other. Null = the coach never stated a contracted number.

members.description: The roster. One entry per seat, past and present — a departed member stays on the roster with status='departed' so history, billing periods, and the member's own arc remain readable. Never pruned.

person_id.description: Canonical person id. Must reference an existing person; the pack resolves through entity_resolve before writing (never a bare name).

status.description: Seat state. 'paused' still holds the seat (and usually still bills); 'departed' does not.

departed_at.description: Required in code when status='departed' — a departure with no date can't be billed to a period boundary.

also_1to1.description: HINT ONLY: this member is also a 1:1 coaching client. The truth is whether a kind='coaching' thread names this person, and coach_state.member_is_also_1to1 derives it that way — this flag is the fallback when no coaching thread has been created yet. Never treated as authoritative (a stored duplicate of a derivable fact is the drift class the typed readers exist to prevent).

billing_target.description: SPEC COACH1 §8.1: who pays for THIS seat. Null means the cohort's own payer (`cohort.billing.payer`) — the common case. Set when one company's person sits in a cohort but is invoiced to their own company rather than the cohort's payer.

materials_thread_id.description: Optional link to the thread holding this cohort's placemat / materials history.

term_end.description: SPEC COACH1 §4.3, cohort side: the contracted end of this cohort's term. A cohort has a term of its own, distinct from any single seat's. Null = no stated term, and renewal watching is OFF for this cohort (stated plainly at enable-coach rather than inferred from silence).

renewal_date.description: When the renewal conversation is due. Usually before `term_end`; null falls back to term_end minus the workspace's coach.renewal_lead_days.

billing.description: SPEC COACH1 §8.1: the cohort's own payer and rate — the default every seat with a null `billing_target` rolls up to. Written by the pack's billing skill in Phase 4; defined here in Phase 1 so `billing_target: null` has a documented referent from the start. Money is user-stated or user-confirmed only, never estimated (quantify.py discipline).

rate.description: Rate per `unit` in `currency`. Null = unknown; an absent rate renders no money figure rather than a guess.

consolidate_by_payer.description: True = one invoice per payer per period, itemized per person and per cohort seat (§8.1 roll-up rule).

id.description: Stable org id. Readable slug preferred (e.g., org_acme_co, org_holding_co).

legal_name.description: Formal registered company name when it differs from canonical_name (e.g. 'Acme Lab Inc.' vs the everyday 'Acme Labs'). Real data — admitted v4.8.1 (F-05) so records carrying it stop failing validation. Matched by org_writer.find_existing_org's name lookup; canonical_name remains the display source of truth.

scope.description: What role this org plays in the tree. 'holding' = top-level parent with operating children. 'operating' = revenue-generating unit. 'division' = sub-unit inside operating. 'brand' = customer-facing label. 'fund' = investment vehicle. 'other' = escape hatch with scope_label.

parent_org_id.description: Parent org for nested structures. Null for top-level entities. No cycles.

relationship_type.description: The CEO's role vs this org. 'operating' = runs it. 'partner' = co-founded/co-owned. 'board' = board seat. 'advisory' = advisor/consultant. 'investment' = holds equity, doesn't run. 'client' = paid engagement. 'portfolio_company' = portco of a fund the CEO runs. 'beneficiary' = family office beneficiary/grantor. 'vendor' = a third party who sells the CEO products/services (added v2.10.3). 'prospect' = a third party in active sales conversation, not yet a client (added v2.10.3). 'service_provider' = a vendor with ongoing relationship — accountant, lawyer, agency (added v2.10.3). 'other' = escape hatch with relationship_label.

tier.description: Visual + filtering tier (added v2.10.3). 'primary' = the CEO's own org(s) — holding + operating units they run. Renders prominent in Orgs Map; surfaces in every daily flow. 'secondary' = active client/partner/advisor — high-signal external relationships. Renders normally; surfaces in daily flows. 'external' = vendor/prospect/service_provider — low-signal third parties. Renders smaller / under collapsed External section in Orgs Map; only surfaces in daily flows when there's an open commitment or a meeting on the calendar. 'passive' = dormant/archived/orphan — historical reference only. Hidden from daily flows; accessible by name. Tier is set by inference rules at onboarding (primary-affiliation gate + interaction-volume thresholds) or explicitly by the user.

is_primary_focus.description: Bubbles this org to the top of briefings. Multiple orgs can be primary focus (portfolio/holding-co operators).

domains.description: Email/web domains associated with this org. Used for connector-driven discovery and aliasing.

inferred_from.description: What signals led to this org's existence in the registry. Supports weekly-audit boundary and drift checks.

type.description: DEPRECATED. Use relationship_type + is_primary_focus. Legacy values: 'home' | 'side' | 'personal'.

needs_enrichment.description: Provisional org from reactive discovery, awaiting CEO confirm (deep-audit #18). On-entity flag; cleared on confirm. Replaces the forbidden pending_review.

money.description: SPEC HIST1 Part A: recurring account/revenue money for this org — the fallback quantify.money_time_tag reads when an item has no deal.value (an org can have both; the stated per-deal figure still wins on deal-thread items). Inner keys are EXACTLY the conventional names in quantify._MONEY_FIELDS so the grouped object resolves through _money_part's candidate list. Written ONLY via org_writer.set_org_money(confirmed=True) — reachable only from an explicit user statement or a confirmed brain_proposal; NEVER estimated, never auto (Bug #92 / PIPE1 D9 money discipline). Absent money = no dollar tag, exactly as before.

account_value.description: Recurring account value in `currency` (e.g. 120000 for a $120k/yr account). User-stated or confirmed only.

revenue.description: Known revenue figure for the relationship. User-stated or confirmed only.

arr.description: Annual recurring revenue. User-stated or confirmed only.

mrr.description: Monthly recurring revenue. User-stated or confirmed only.

source.description: Where the figure came from — 'user statement', 'confirmed proposal', 'QBO sales-by-customer', … Required in code by set_org_money (money is always sourced).

brand.description: OPTIONAL, DORMANT per-org deliverable theme (SPEC OUT1). Overrides the workspace brand for documents scoped to THIS org (via make_brief org_id=). Absent = the workspace brand (or premium defaults). Set by hand during a paid customization engagement; never touched by onboarding.

engagement.description: A non-ownership edge between two orgs (fund engagement, portfolio company, deal, advisory, vendor, etc.). The orgs map renderer surfaces these under the from-org as 'Engaged with:' rows, visually distinct from owned children. Engaged orgs remain at top level — engagements form a graph, not a tree.

id.description: Stable engagement id. Sequential: engagement_001, engagement_002, …

from_org_id.description: The engaging org (the one that 'has' the relationship). Must reference an existing org id.

to_org_id.description: The target org (the one being engaged with). Must reference an existing org id.

kind.description: Initial taxonomy. Renderer treats unknown kinds as generic 'engaged with'.

label.description: Short display label, e.g., 'Fund-level partnership', 'Pilot deal — AP automation'.

notes.description: Free-text context. Surfaced in tooltips / detail views.

ended_at.description: When the engagement ACTUALLY ended (backward-looking). Distinct from `term_end`, which is the contracted end date and may sit in the future on a live engagement.

term_end.description: SPEC COACH1 §4.3: the contracted end of the current term — forward-looking, and set while the engagement is still live. Renewal watching reads this instead of leaning on the dormancy heuristic: a coaching term has a real end date, so `dormant-customer-scan`'s pattern gets reused against a real date rather than inferred silence. Null = no stated term, and renewal watching is OFF for this engagement (said plainly at setup, never guessed). Additive and optional — every existing engagement record stays valid unchanged.

renewal_date.description: SPEC COACH1 §4.3: when the renewal conversation is due. Usually earlier than `term_end`; null falls back to term_end minus the workspace's coach.renewal_lead_days.

is_active.description: Inactive engagements are filtered from the renderer.

workspace_settings.description: Per-workspace user/locale/onboarding settings. Lives at top-level `workspace` field of entities.json. All fields optional; readers handle missing fields with sensible defaults.

user_id.description: The primary user's person_id. Used by readers that need to identify whose workspace this is (Friday Wrap internal/external split, dormancy live-check self-reply filter, etc.). Canonical signal — preferred over the legacy `is_primary_user: true` person field.

user_timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. America/New_York). Read by tz.py to_local() for workspace-local date math. Falls back to UTC if missing — but missing should be filled by command-room-onboarding Step 1c.

first_go_months.description: How many months back the user wants the initial backfill to cover at first install. Set by command-room-onboarding Step 1c. Optional after first install.

schedule_timezone.description: Timezone used by scheduled tasks. Usually identical to user_timezone but can be set separately for cases where the user travels.

brand.description: OPTIONAL, DORMANT deliverable theme applied to ALL of this workspace's .docx output (SPEC OUT1). Absent = premium defaults. Set by hand during a paid customization engagement; never touched by onboarding.

personal_calendars.description: SPEC BAL1 D5. The declared personal/family calendar ids (personal Google primary, shared family calendar, or an ICS feed id) the Balance surface reads for open evenings. Calendar-specific — deliberately NOT the mail-keyed workspace.accounts[]. Absent/empty = Balance refuses honestly (not-configured != healthy). Set via workspace-manager; read-only calendars unless the user confirms a hold.

evening_start.description: SPEC BAL1 D5. 'HH:MM' start of the protected evening window for open-evening detection (default 18:00).

evening_end.description: SPEC BAL1 D5. 'HH:MM' end of the evening window (default 22:00).

min_block_hours.description: SPEC BAL1 D5. Minimum free-block length (hours) for an evening to count as open (default 2).

balance_default_cadence_days.description: SPEC BAL1 D2. Default personal re-surface cadence (days) for a tie with no cadence_days of its own (default 14). Read only by shared/scripts/balance.py.

coach.description: SPEC COACH1 §4.4: the coach pack's workspace block. ABSENT on every non-coach workspace, and absence is the off switch — `coach_state.get_coach_config` returns {} and every coach surface stays silent. Written at enable-coach (Phase 2) through shared/scripts/workspace_settings.py so the `workspace_setting_changed` receipt can never separate from the write. Values here are the workspace-wide DEFAULTS; a per-engagement value on the thread always wins, and a per-skill knob in _hq/data/skill_config/<skill>.json wins over both.

enabled.description: Master switch. False (or the whole block absent) = the pack's scheduled passes and surfaces do nothing. Set true only when enable-coach has completed.

practice_name.description: The coaching practice's own name, as the coach says it. Used in member-facing artifacts (§9) — never a Chalette or Command Room string.

default_session_minutes.description: Default scheduled session length. Per-engagement value wins. Feeds the billable-unit derivation when the calendar event carries no duration.

default_cadence_days.description: Default days between sessions (e.g. 30 for monthly). Drives the prep/capture pass anchors and the 'a session was missed' read. Per-engagement cadence wins.

renewal_lead_days.description: How far before `term_end` a renewal window opens when no explicit `renewal_date` is set. The one derived-date default, kept here so the number is stated once.

report_output_shape.description: §5.2. `file_per_session` (default) writes one record per session. `single_running_document` appends newest-first to one file — SHIPS, but only via the atomic-write path with a per-session copy kept alongside so the running doc is always reconstructible. A plain read-modify-write append on Drive-synced storage loses history when a stale second machine writes (§5.3 — a known clobber pattern in this system, not a hypothetical).

personal_thread_split.description: §5.1 / §12. True = follow-up and action items render work and personal separately. The SPLIT is a knob; the personal/business FIREWALL is not — it holds either way.

attribution_footer.description: §9.3 (OPEN — M's ruling pending): one restrained attribution line in the footer of member-facing artifacts. Default on; flipping the default is this one value and nothing else.

billing.description: §8.1 workspace-wide billing defaults. Per-engagement and per-seat values win. Rate is user-stated only — never estimated.

invoice_posture.description: M ruling 7, and the ONLY legal value in v1: the draft assembles automatically, the coach confirms EACH invoice, one confirm sends one invoice. There is deliberately no batch or scheduled auto-send value to select — the enum is single-valued so a future 'auto' can only be added by a deliberate schema change.

qbo_connected.description: §8.4. False = the tally, the unbilled-contact confirmation pass, and an exportable invoice-ready summary all still work; only the send step is unavailable. Billing must never present a dead surface to a coach who never connects QuickBooks.

hero_template_ref.description: §7.3. Workspace-relative path to the coach's own session-record template (conventionally _hq/coach/templates/session_record.md). Null = the shipped hero template. Once supplied it is NEVER ours — same posture as advisor_profile: read, never rewritten.

placemat_template_ref.description: §7.3. Workspace-relative path to the coach's own group-placemat template. Null = the shipped default.
